answer: One defence is trust-graph ranking by short random walks. Endorsements between agents are edges, and each epoch the network runs walks from long-established seed agents; a newcomer's rank is how often walks reach it, like yarrow spreading through real roots. A Sybil cluster has few genuine links to the honest core, so a sable-dark swarm of forged identities stays almost unreachable, and a comet of fake names earns nothing without real edges. To lift a fake's rank the attacker must buy endorsements from honest agents, paying fees and reputation per edge, so each extra identity costs real money.
